## title: "Policy Work"

My policy work applies to key questions facing Alaska. Much of this work focuses on energy, natural resources, public finance, and regional economic conditions.

Projects range from short-form economic analysis and policy briefs to longer research reports, legislative testimony, and collaborative work with public agencies and private organizations.

## Alaska Economy

I regularly analyze economic conditions in Alaska, including employment, wages, inflation, energy prices, resource markets, and state revenues.

Current and recent work includes:

* statewide and regional employment trends
* oil prices and petroleum production
* household energy costs
* inflation and real wage growth
* tourism and transportation activity
* state revenue and fiscal conditions

## Energy

My energy policy work focuses on Alaska's natural gas and electricity markets, energy infrastructure, and the state's relationship to broader Pacific energy markets.

### Cook Inlet Natural Gas

Analysis of declining Cook Inlet gas production, potential LNG imports, demand-side responses, renewable generation, and alternative sources of long-run gas supply.

[Read more](#)

### Alaska LNG

Research and policy analysis examining the economics of North Slope natural gas development and LNG exports, including construction costs, breakeven prices, global LNG supply, and long-run Pacific market conditions.

[Read more](#)

### Energy Prices and Households

Analysis of gasoline, natural gas, electricity, and other energy costs and their implications for Alaska households and businesses.

[Read more](#)

## Fisheries

My fisheries policy work examines commercial fishing institutions, ownership, participation, and the economic conditions facing fishing communities.

Topics include:

* commercial fishing permit ownership
* local and non-local participation
* fishing income and permit values
* demographic change
* processing infrastructure
* owner-operator requirements
* community economic impacts

[Selected fisheries work](#)

## Mining & Critical Minerals

My work on mining and critical minerals examines both project-level economics and broader mineral supply chains.

Recent topics include:

* mine development and permitting
* critical mineral supply chains
* mine waste and tailings reprocessing
* mineral processing and refining
* mine ownership and productivity
* infrastructure constraints
* regional economic impacts
* opportunities for Alaska within domestic mineral supply chains

[Selected mining and critical-minerals work](#)

## Public Finance

I conduct applied research on Alaska's state and local public finances, particularly the interaction between resource revenues, taxation, public spending, and long-run fiscal sustainability.

Topics include:

* petroleum revenues
* state revenue forecasts
* sales and income taxation
* Permanent Fund earnings
* the Permanent Fund Dividend
* energy rebates
* state spending
* fiscal sustainability

[Selected public finance work](#)

I regularly communicate economic research to policymakers, journalists, industry groups, and the public.
